title: Minimax Estimation of the Causal Mann-Whitney Probability under Low Regularity
banked_reason: The promised low-regularity minimax frontier is not delivered: the feasible O(r_n) upper remains open while the proved results supply only a separated lower/first-order-upper bracket.
gap_reasons: The promised low-regularity minimax frontier is not delivered: this node leaves the feasible O(r_n) upper (and hence sharp same-class minimax characterization) open, while the proved results supply only a separated lower/first-order-upper bracket; retain it as an honest partial result or supply the missing feasible sharp upper before claiming the frontier.
The r_n oracle uses unknown population kernels, while the feasible higher-order candidate has no proved risk bound.

Repair requires a genuinely new proof controlling fitted inverse-Gram corrections, hyperbolically omitted-string bias, and all paired Hoeffding overlaps, or an equally sharp same-class frontier impossibility theorem.
proof_attempt_summary: The run developed and audited a paired higher-order signed-law route, proved a same-class binary lower bound, a feasible first-order upper bound, a matched root-n sufficient region, and a sharp population-oracle benchmark. Finite-grid chain calculations exposed nonvanishing truncated Gram remainders, and repeated maximality passes could not turn the oracle construction into a feasible O(r_n) estimator. The remaining task is a new proof of fitted inverse-Gram control, hyperbolically omitted-string bias, and every paired two-arm Hoeffding-overlap bound, or a same-class impossibility theorem that closes the frontier in the opposite direction.
tldr: For the independent-draw half-tie causal Mann--Whitney probability with bounded ordered outcomes and arbitrary atoms, we prove a feasible first-order upper bound for every positive smoothness triple. When \(4\alpha\beta\ge d^2\), it matches the parametric lower bound and yields a uniform fixed-radius root-\(n\) interval, including at zero-gradient-variance laws. Below the elbow, for every \(0<\gamma\le\alpha\), we prove a same-class binary lower and feasible polynomial upper bracket. A population-kernel four-block oracle reaches \(r_n\), but a feasible \(O(r_n)\) paired upper, equality-elbow upper, and efficiency theorem remain unresolved.
gap: First-order causal rank theory does not determine low-regularity minimax risk. Scalar higher-order estimators do not automatically control the random score created by the other intervention law.
fill: Audit and, if valid, prove the explicit cross-fitted two-arm higher-order estimator, establish its same-class binary lower bound, and separate the compatible minimax rate from asymmetric and equality-elbow questions.
